verdict.rationale: ROS 2 documents QoS settings built for non-ideal networks. Its transient-local durability has publishers persist samples for late-joining subscribers, and rosbag lets nodes record data locally, which together give some local buffering and reconnection behaviour. Nothing in the evidence addresses cloud connectivity loss, store-and-forward upload, or clean recovery as a packaged capability; operators must assemble it from these primitives. missing for 10: documented offline/cloud-disconnect operation, store-and-forward sync of buffered data to cloud on reconnect, documented recovery semantics after network partitions, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops lead, my robots keep operating and buffer data locally when cloud connectivity drops, then recover cleanly

citations.quote: Quality of service settings for handling non-ideal networks
Transient local: the publisher becomes responsible for persisting samples for "late-joining" subscriptions.
This allows you to subscribe to a topic and save the received data to a bag at the same time as performing any other processing of your choice on that data.
